page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.t5-c1m4.xlarge is a burstable server instance based on the x86_64 architecture and powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at 2.5 GHz. Managed via a KVM hypervisor, the instance provides 4 vCPUs distributed across 2 physical cores using hyperthreading. It features 16 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB per vCPU, along with 33 MB of L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AVX-512F, AES, BMI2, ADX, and FMA. The instance comes without bundled local storage and maintains a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks reflect low compute and memory throughput consistent with its burstable allocation profile. In synthetic testing, the instance achieved a stress-ng single-core score of 994.99 and a multi-core score of 4027.78. Geekbench scores reached 806.0 for single-core and 2327.0 for multi-core performance. Memory bandwidth benchmarks recorded 28.92 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 26.44 GB/sec for uncached large-block writes. Operational workload metrics include a Redis SET performance of 4.15 million operations per second and a static web serving throughput of 2.53 GB/sec.

The burstable resource allocation makes this instance a budget-conscious entry for workloads with intermittent compute demands. Because sustained CPU execution is credit-constrained, continuous heavy compute tasks experience performance limitations. The provision of 16 GB RAM alongside modest burstable CPU performance fits lightweight microservices, development and testing environments, low-traffic web applications, and low-duty background processing.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.t5-c1m4.xlarge is a burstable virtual machine built on the x86_64 architecture, featuring an Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. Configured with 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores and 16 GB of memory (4 GB per vCPU), the instance operates on a KVM hypervisor with an L3 cache of 33 MB. It lacks local storage and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps. Benchmark results demonstrate weak-to-poor performance across synthetic CPU and memory metrics, recording a single-core stress-ng score of 994.99, a Geekbench multi-core score of 2327.0, and a Redis SET throughput of 4.15 million operations per second. Extended cryptographic and vector processing features like AVX-512 and AES are supported, though absolute throughput remains low. The burstable CPU allocation offers a cost-effective profile for low-duty microservices, staging environments, build servers with periodic CPU spikes, and lightweight web applications rather than sustained compute-intensive workloads.
